title: A Physics‐Based, Lumped‐Parameter Model for Attributing Natural and Anthropogenic CO2 Emissions From Producing Geothermal Systems
content:
Abstract

Although geothermal energy is a low-carbon resource, some powerplants can coproduce and release CO2 ${\text{CO}}_{2}$, which is then subject to emissions monitoring and sometimes financial penalty. Accurate attribution of these emissions is difficult because exploitation of the reservoir alters hydrological flows that in turn modify surface CO2 ${\text{CO}}_{2}$ fluxes. Hence, emissions metered through the powerplant do not represent the true anthropogenic impact. This study develops a lumped-parameter model of a geothermal reservoir that tracks pressure evolution, dissolved CO2 ${\text{CO}}_{2}$ and emissions through the powerplant and the Earth's surface. Closed-form analytical solutions are obtained for reservoir degassing, outflow reversal, delayed reinjection returns and mineralization reactions, and these are calibrated against emissions data from the Rotokawa and Ngā Tamariki geothermal fields in New Zealand. The interplay of characteristic timescales for pressure equilibration, CO2 ${\text{CO}}_{2}$ loss, reservoir residence, breakthrough delay and mineralization are shown to control whether a field's emissions decline, stabilize or rebound over decades. Calibrated models indicate that plant-metered emissions at Rotokawa overcount the true anthropogenic impact by 17–45 kt yr−1 ${\text{yr}}^{-1}$, because production suppresses surface emissions that are not credited to the operator. CO2 ${\text{CO}}_{2}$ storage in geothermal reservoirs is shown to be fundamentally different from conventional carbon capture and storage, as it is a flow-through system in which dissolved CO2 ${\text{CO}}_{2}$ only resides temporarily. Long-term sequestration requires either mineralization or reinjection at sufficient distance to delay returns. Field-specific models and repeat CO2 ${\text{CO}}_{2}$ flux surveys are needed to constrain these effects and support emissions accounting based on true anthropogenic impact.
